source_passage_locator: K055S02: Pease et al. Insights into epileptogenesis from post-traumatic epilepsy → Introduction; Risk factors for PTE; Epileptogenesis in PTE → Mechanisms; Figure 2 and caption
review_note: Reviewed K055S01 and K055S02. K055S02 explicitly describes TBI as an initiating insult that can produce structural damage and initiate chronic epileptogenesis involving neuroinflammation, blood-brain barrier dysfunction and epileptogenic circuit remodeling. This supports Traumatic brain injury → Structural brain injury and epileptogenic remodeling as a possible causal mechanism. K055S01 establishes structural injury but not the complete remodeling component and remains partial. Not every TBI produces epileptogenic remodeling. AI-assisted review; human confirmation pending.

effect_node: Higher risk of recurrent unprovoked seizures (post-traumatic epilepsy)
source_passage_locator: K055S03: Pease et al. Insights into epileptogenesis from post-traumatic epilepsy → Risk factors for PTE; Epileptogenesis in PTE → Mechanisms; Figure 2 and caption; Early PTSs and PTE
review_note: Reviewed K055S03 and K055S04. K055S03 directly describes how injury-associated neuronal loss, gliosis, neuroinflammation and neural circuit reorganization contribute to epileptogenesis and increased susceptibility to later spontaneous unprovoked seizures. This supports Structural brain injury and epileptogenic remodeling → Higher risk of recurrent unprovoked seizures (post-traumatic epilepsy) as RISK_FACTOR_FOR. K055S04 supports abnormal post-injury nerve connections and seizures but does not establish the complete late-PTE relationship, so it remains partial and is excluded from supporting_source_ids. Early provoked seizures within seven days are not equivalent to later unprovoked post-traumatic seizures. AI-assisted review; human confirmation pending.
